q: A single neuron ŷ = σ(w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + b) has what kind of decision boundary?
why: The boundary is w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + b = 0, a line (Eq. 2).

wrong.2: Any monotone σ thresholds the same linear function.

q: A 5-layer network with identity activations is no more expressive than a single linear layer.
why: Composition of linear maps is linear.

q: Maximum value of the sigmoid derivative σ'(z)?
Shape of W⁽ℓ⁾ in the slides' convention?
why: z = h W + b with h a row vector of length n_{ℓ−1} (Eq. 10, 13).

q: Which loss/output pairs give output error δ = ŷ − y? (select all)

wrong.3: MSE + sigmoid keeps a σ'(z) factor.

wrong.0: Missing the transpose and the activation derivative.
wrong.2: That is the weight gradient form.

q: Compared with numerical differentiation, backprop's cost is roughly…
why: One forward + one backward pass of similar cost (p.38).

q: Best default activation for hidden layers?
Training loss ↓ while validation loss ↑ indicates…
Biases should be initialised randomly to break symmetry.
why: Biases start at zero; random weights break symmetry (p.55).

q:
Shapes: H is (64, 128), W is (128, 32), b is (32,).
What is the shape of H @ W + b ?
why: B × n_ℓ, with the bias broadcast across rows (Eq. 17).
